resources.string: Tap once to latch a modifier on; tap again to turn off. Highlighted keys show what is latched. Good for typing shifted symbols with a separate tap on Shift, then the key.
Short tap sends that modifier key once to the target. Long-press a modifier, keep your finger down, then tap other keys to chord (e.g. long-press Shift and tap 1 for !). Release the modifier to stop.
Hold modifier on target while chording

Sends a real modifier-down to the connected device when you long-press, and keeps it applied after each chorded key until you lift your finger. Turn off only if your host misbehaves with sustained modifiers.
After a short delay, sends many quick press-and-release cycles—similar to auto-repeat when holding a physical key for typing.
Hold key down on the target
Sends one key-down when you press and releases when you lift your finger. Better for games or apps that expect a real held key instead of repeated taps.

Long text can lose characters on some target devices due to HID transmission limits.

To type non-ASCII characters on the target Mac, add the input source “Unicode Hex Input” (System Settings → Keyboard → Input Sources → Edit → + → English → Unicode Hex Input) and select it in the menu bar before you send.

This app sends the same Option-held hex digit sequence as Voice Input: hold Option (Alt), then type four hex digits (0–9 and A–F). For example U+5C0A is typed as 5, C, 0, A.

Hex uses letters A–F. macOS and third-party tools often assign shortcuts to Option+letter (for example Option+A may open an app or take a screenshot). If a shortcut fires instead of entering a hex digit, that character will be wrong or missing. On the target Mac, turn off or reassign conflicting shortcuts under System Settings → Keyboard → Keyboard Shortcuts, and check utilities that register Option shortcuts.

If one character fails but another succeeds, Unicode Hex Input is usually active but a specific digit (often A–F) is being intercepted—adjust the target Mac until Option+hex matches manual entry.

To verify Option+hex on the Mac without sending your compose message, open this help again and tap Test Unicode hex path (the second action beside OK on this dialog).
On the target Windows PC, this option sends Alt+numpad-plus and hex digits (Unicode entry). Ensure a layout with a working numeric keypad path is available on the target.
On the target Linux host, this option sends Ctrl+Shift+U followed by hex digits and Enter (typical IBus/GTK Unicode entry). Ensure that shortcut is accepted by the focused application.
On the target device, enable the OS-specific Unicode entry method that matches the selected target OS before using this option.

On the target Mac: open a plain scratch document in TextEdit or similar (not an important email or IDE buffer).

Select the input source Unicode Hex Input and place the caret in the field you will watch.

Wrong input source or missing fonts can show a different glyph or a tofu box—that is not always a shortcut hijack. If Unicode Hex Input is active and the character still does not match after Retry, treat it as likely hijack, focus loss, or a transport issue.
